title: LaDiR: Latent Diffusion Enhances LLMs for Text Reasoning
claim: Existing reasoning paradigms generate tokens sequentially or via masked discrete diffusion; ours iteratively refines blocks of continuous latent thoughts.
layout: 3 stacked panels: baselines top, ours bottom, legend right; left-to-right flows
description: A figure comparing reasoning paradigms. The top-left panel shows two autoregressive rows: AR CoT, a chain from Q through blue text tokens x1..xL to [Answer], and AR Latent CoT (Coconut), with green continuous tokens h1..hL. The top-right panel shows Diffusion LMs (Blockwise), where stacked purple layers in rounded Block 1 and Block 2 go from [MASK]...[MASK] at t=T to filled tokens at t=0, ending in stacked answers. A horizontal line separates the bottom panel, LaDiR. There, Q feeds stacked orange-pink blocks of latent thought tokens z, then more blocks, then stacked answers. A dashed arrow leads to a noise-to-clean denoising strip from t=T to t=0. A legend on the right explains the token types and noise. The eye goes first to the baselines at the top, then to the colorful LaDiR row below.
caption: Comparison of reasoning paradigms: autoregressive CoT and latent CoT generate discrete or continuous tokens sequentially; diffusion LMs iteratively convert [MASK] tokens to discrete text tokens in parallel in a semi-autoregressive way; and our proposed method LaDiR reasons over latent thought tokens via diffusion, enabling iterative refinement at semantic level and diverse exploration.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate their reasoning ability through chain-of-thought (CoT) generation. However, LLM's autoregressive decoding may limit the ability to revisit and refine earlier tokens in a holistic manner, which can also lead to inefficient exploration for diverse solutions. In this paper, we propose LaDiR} (Latent Diffusion Reasoner), a novel reasoning framework that unifies the expressiveness of continuous latent representation with the iterative refinement capabilities of latent diffusion models for an existing LLM. We first construct a structured latent reasoning space using a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) that encodes text reasoning steps into blocks of thought tokens, preserving semantic information and interpretability while offering compact but expressive representations. Subsequently, we utilize a latent diffusion model that learns to denoise a block of latent thought tokens with a blockwise bidirectional attention mask, enabling longer horizon and iterative refinement with adaptive test-time compute. This design, combined with explicit diversity guidance during diffusion inference, enables the generation of multiple diverse reasoning trajectories that explore distinct regions of the latent space, rather than producing repetitive solutions as often occurs in standard autoregressive sampling. We conduct evaluations on a suite of mathematical reasoning, code generation and puzzle planning benchmarks. Empirical results show that LaDiR consistently improves accuracy, diversity, and interpretability over existing autoregressive, diffusion-based, and latent reasoning methods, revealing a new paradigm for text reasoning with latent diffusion.
